input: Upgrade the home security camera system this month

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether this means replacing existing cameras, adding new ones, upgrading software/firmware, or overhauling the entire system changes the entire plan.
Whether this is a DIY project or involves hiring a professional installer determines the steps, timeline, and costs involved.
The size of the property and the specific areas to be covered (indoor, outdoor, entrances, garage) dictate the number of cameras and placement strategy.
The budget sets hard limits on which camera systems, brands, and features are realistic options.
Preferred features (e.g., wired vs. wireless, cloud vs. local storage, smart home integration, night vision, resolution) heavily influence which products to choose.
Whether the user already has a system in place (and what brand/type) determines compatibility requirements and whether existing infrastructure can be reused.
Understanding what a successful upgrade looks like — better coverage, fewer blind spots, remote access, deterrence — ensures the plan is evaluated against the right outcome.

gold.taskTitle: Upgrade home security camera system this month
gold.taskDescription: Plan and execute a full upgrade of the user's home security camera system within the current month.

questions.title: Are you replacing cameras, adding more, or upgrading software?
questions.description: Clarify whether the upgrade involves swapping out existing hardware, expanding coverage with new cameras, updating firmware/apps, or a complete system overhaul.

questions.title: Will you install everything yourself or hire a professional?
questions.description: Determine if this is a DIY project or if a professional installer will be involved, which affects timeline, cost, and task steps.

questions.title: Which specific areas of your home need camera coverage?
questions.description: Identify the locations to be covered — front door, backyard, garage, interior rooms — and the scale of the property to estimate camera count and placement.

questions.title: What is your total budget for this upgrade?
questions.description: Establish a hard budget ceiling to filter realistic product and installation options.

questions.title: Do you prefer wired or wireless cameras for this setup?
questions.description: Understand the user's preference for wired (PoE) vs. wireless (Wi-Fi/battery) systems, which drives product selection and installation complexity.

questions.title: Do you already have a security system or cameras installed?
questions.description: Determine if existing hardware or infrastructure is in place, what brand or ecosystem it belongs to, and whether it can be reused or must be replaced.

questions.title: What does a successful upgrade look like when you are done?
questions.description: Define the end goal — e.g., no blind spots, remote viewing on phone, motion alerts, local storage — so the plan can be evaluated against the right outcome.
